h: When Eating Meat Serves the Desire of the Soul

p: כִּי יַרְחִיב ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת גְּבוּלְךָ וְגוֹמֵר
"When Hashem your God enlarges your border," etc.;
בְּכָל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר (דְּבָרִים יב, כ)
"you may eat meat, whatever your soul desires" (Devarim 12:20).
that one should not eat meat
except out of plenty and wealth."
This implies that out of wealth
one is permitted to eat meat for appetite.
But seemingly, it is explicit in Scripture
"The meat was still between their teeth," etc.,
כִּי שָׁם קָבְרוּ אֶת הָעָם הַמִּתְאַוִּים
"for there they buried the people that lusted."
In truth, the words of Rashi, of blessed memory,
and so it is in the Sifrei (Sifrei Devarim 75).
that here, in the pesukim of this parshah,
we see that they were precise in the wording:
"because your soul desires to eat meat,
you may eat meat, whatever your soul desires";
"and you shall eat within your gates,
whatever your soul desires" — you may eat meat;
all in terms of the soul.
that it needs the eating of meat
for the attainment of words of Torah.
It is like what we find of Rav Nachman
"for I had not eaten ox meat";
"I did not examine the reason of the matter precisely";
that he had not eaten meat,
that he needed the meat for his Torah study;
וּכְעֵין שֶׁאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן לְעִנְיַן הַיַּיִן
similar to what Rav Nachman said regarding wine
"As long as I have not drunk
And this is what Rashi explained,
"I did not examine the reason of the matter precisely":
since he had not eaten meat,
לֹא יָכוֹל לְדַקְדֵּק טַעְמוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר
he could not examine the reason of the matter precisely;
the eating of meat and the drinking of wine
Now, in the Sifrei there is a dispute between
אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר לָהֶם בְּשַׂר תַּאֲוָה וְכוּלֵּי
to permit them meat of appetite, etc.;
to forbid them meat of an animal killed by stabbing.
what was said, "One may always slaughter,"
as referring to the present time,
that in the present time meat of appetite is forbidden;
"It should have said, 'One may always slaughter and eat'!
Because they were near the Mishkan;
and in the end why were they permitted?
Because they were far from the Mishkan;
when they are even farther from it."
it explains it according to Rabbi Akiva:
for meat killed by stabbing is not permitted.
וְהִנֵּה בַּפָּסוּק יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן כֶּפֶל
Now in the pasuk there is also a repetition:
first it is written, "When He enlarges," etc.,
"you may eat meat, whatever your soul desires,"
"and you shall eat within your gates,
In its plain sense, it implies
דְּוְכִי יִרְחַק קָאֵי עַל חוּץ לָאָרֶץ
that "if it be too far" refers to outside the Land;
and if so, one may also ask:
מָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּתַּר בְּשַׂר תַּאֲוָה
if in Eretz Yisrael meat of appetite was permitted
because they were far from the Mishkan,
all the more so outside the Land,
There is also a superfluous phrase,
"you shall slaughter of your cattle and of your flock
וְלָמָּה כָּתַב אֲשֶׁר נָתַן ה׳ לְךָ
why did it write "which Hashem has given you"?
But according to our words it is well:
כִּי יַרְחִיב ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת גְּבוּלְךָ וְגוֹמֵר
"When Hashem your God enlarges your border," etc.,
"you may eat meat, whatever your soul desires"
that is, the holiness of Eretz Yisrael was effective
that the eating be in holiness,
and that the eating of meat be
only a desire of the soul
"If the place be too far from you," etc.,
וְשָׁם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִסְמוֹךְ עַל זֶה
and there one cannot rely on this,
that the desire is a desire of the soul
and not a lust of the body.
"you shall slaughter of your cattle and of your flock,"
which is expounded (in the Sifrei and the Gemara, Chullin 84a):
"of your cattle — and not all your cattle," etc.;
וְגַם פֵּרַט אֲשֶׁר נָתַן ה׳ לְךָ
It also specified "which Hashem has given you";
and it is as we said,
that Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, asked
"and will give me bread to eat";
should also be the One who feeds;
from the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He,
it does not lead to lust
and the evil inclination, Heaven forbid.
who was the son-in-law of the Nasi's house
that meat and wine were his allotted bread,
which Hashem Yisbarach had allotted him,
since he needed it for his Torah study.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And as Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him, asked
that Hashem Yisbarach should be the One who provides,
and he would have his allotted bread,
according to what he needed for words of Torah;
And it said "as I have commanded you"
to eat, that is, eating in holiness
"And you shall eat within your gates,
is a spiritual longing, a desire of the soul.
let them set a pot on the fire for him every day."
וְהַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מֵאָה מָנֶה
That is, one who has a hundred maneh,
whom Hashem has graced with wealth
it is clear that the meat
which he needs for words of Torah.
From Shabbos eve to Shabbos eve";
the eating is always in holiness,
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת אַף אִם אוֹכֵל לְתַאֲוַת גּוּפוֹ
that on Shabbos, even if one eats for his body's desire,
And this is what they said in the holy Zohar
"'The dung of your festivals,' it says,
and not 'the dung of your Shabbosos'";
for on Shabbos there is no refuse in the eating,
אִינּוּן כְּשַׁבָּתוֹת (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג כט, ב)
for their eating is always in holiness;
and one who knows in his soul
that he needs the meat for words of Torah
"We must be concerned for the words of the elder"
for he did not trust himself,
lest his eating be bodily lust
and not the desire of the soul,
and it is permitted to him
for the root of his soul, for words of Torah.
שֶׁרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אָמַר סְתָם
For Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah spoke without qualification,
that there is concern even in Shabbos eating
for one who is not permitted
to be concerned even on Shabbos
lest he not intend it for the mitzvah.
"Abba was of a family of healthy people," etc.,
he could be stringent with himself;
should run with it to the shopkeeper,"
is needed by him for the Torah,
and it is like the eating of Shabbos.
that meat was his allotted bread,
מִמַּה שֶּׁנָּתַן לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׁר
from the fact that Hashem Yisbarach gave him wealth,
one who knows in his soul
that he needs meat for words of Torah
even if he has no wealth,
the precision of the pesukim is well explained.
where it wished to explain it according to Rabbi Yishmael,
that in the present time it was not forbidden
"It should have said, 'One may always slaughter and eat'!"
is the permission to eat meat of appetite;
surely at the time it was permitted
And further, even if we explain
that what they said, "one may always slaughter,"
means the same as "slaughter and eat,"
surely it is a kal vachomer!
And here the novelty was not mentioned
that it is possible to eat in holiness;
if so, how is it fitting
to the wording "one may always slaughter."
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי מוֹקֵי לָהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
Therefore it explains it according to Rabbi Akiva,
that in the wilderness meat killed by stabbing was permitted to them,
that in the present time it is forbidden
But the precision of the pesukim
according to Rabbi Yishmael as well,
And on Shabbos the eating is always in holiness,
and there is no distance of place at all,
there is the holiness of Eretz Yisrael and Yerushalayim,
"Who spreads a shelter of peace over us
and over all His people Yisrael
And they can always eat in holiness.
meat is also permitted to them,
according to the words of Torah.
וְזֶה דִּקְדּוּק לְשׁוֹן רַשִׁ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
And this is the precision of Rashi's words, of blessed memory:
"that a person should not desire to eat meat
except out of plenty and wealth."
בִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּבְרַב נַחְמָן
of Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him, and of Rav Nachman.
And also wealth in words of Torah,
in the manner of what they said
"But the satiety of the rich," etc.
"I speak of those rich in Torah,
and not of those rich in money," etc.
"The rich and the poor meet together" (Mishlei 22:2)
as referring to the wise and the foolish.
וּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עוֹשֶׁר בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
And one who has wealth in words of Torah,
and is confident that he needs the meat
meat is also permitted to him,
רַק רַב מַחְמִיר עַל עַצְמוֹ הָיָה
only Rav was stringent with himself,

rich.text: “שוא  ודבר כזב הרחק ממני ראש ועשר אל תתן לי הטריפני לחם חקי”
— “Keep lies and false words far from me; Give me neither poverty nor riches, But provide me with my daily bread,”

paragraphs.text: Source: Midrash Tanchuma 3:1 — “… תנחומא בר אבא: מתוקה שנת העבד אם מעט ואם הרבה יאכל, והשבע לעשיר איננו מניח לו לישון (קהלת ה, יא). אמרו לו לשלמה: אלו אחר אמר הפסוק הזה, היינו שוחקין …”

rich.text: “… תנחומא בר אבא: מתוקה שנת העבד אם מעט ואם הרבה יאכל, והשבע לעשיר איננו מניח לו לישון (קהלת ה, יא). אמרו לו לשלמה: אלו אחר אמר הפסוק הזה, היינו שוחקין …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Koheles 5:11 — “מתוקה שנת העבד אם מעט ואם הרבה יאכל והשבע לעשיר איננו מניח לו לישון” — “Workers’ sleep is sweet, whether they have much or little to eat; but the abundance of the rich doesn’t let them sleep.”

rich.text: “מתוקה שנת העבד אם מעט ואם הרבה יאכל והשבע לעשיר איננו מניח לו לישון”
— “Workers’ sleep is sweet, whether they have much or little to eat; but the abundance of the rich doesn’t let them sleep.”

paragraphs.text: Source: Mishlei 22:2 — “עשיר ורש נפגשו עשה כלם יהוה” — “The rich and the poor meet; GOD made them both.”

rich.text: — “The rich and the poor meet; GOD made them both.”
